title: Weather forecast for Rio de Janeiro predicts rain and cold front
seoTitle: Weather forecast for Rio de Janeiro predicts rain and.
subtitle: Meteorological data indicate temperature swings and moderate to strong winds in the state capital.
excerpt: The weather forecast for Rio de Janeiro shows temperature changes, scattered showers and an approaching cold front over the next few days.
author: Daniele Morais
sourceName: G1, Centro de Operações Rio, Ilha Carioca
contentHtml:
Variations in the weather conditions in Rio de Janeiro are drawing public attention as a cold front approaches and temperatures shift. Forecast bulletins point to periods of sun mixed with clouds, the possibility of rain showers and moderate to strong winds throughout the week.

Forecast for early week and temperature variation

On Monday, meteorological forecasts indicate a sunny sky with many clouds over the city. In the morning, sunshine will break through the cloud cover, while the afternoon and night bring the chance of rain showers. Estimated temperatures for the day range from a low of 20°C to a high of 32°C.

Complementary analyses for Sunday and Monday also show predominantly partly‑cloudy skies with weak to moderate winds reaching speeds of up to 51.9 km/h. On Tuesday, the pattern of sun with many clouds repeats, keeping the chance of rain showers in the afternoon and night.

Approach of a cold front and moderate to strong rain

The approach and passage of a cold front between Tuesday and Wednesday is expected to change the weather in Rio de Janeiro. With this movement, the sky will become mainly cloudy, and moderate to strong rain showers with lightning are forecast from Tuesday afternoon through early Wednesday morning.

From Wednesday morning onward, instability will lessen, yielding isolated light to moderate rain. During Tuesday, winds will reach moderate to strong intensity, with gusts ranging from 18.5 km/h to 76 km/h, accompanied by a drop in city temperatures.

Influence of a high‑pressure system and winds

On earlier stable‑weather days, the city was under the influence of a high‑pressure system. This atmospheric condition kept the sky partly cloudy to clear, with no rain and occasional moderate winds between 18.5 km/h and 51.9 km/h.

Under this high‑pressure scenario, thermometers recorded high marks, with a minimum temperature of 19°C and a maximum reaching 39.9°C during that period.

Coastal swell warning and maritime conditions

During other unstable periods of the week, the city recorded temperatures between 15°C and 24°C with cloudy to overcast skies. Subsequently, temperatures rose gradually, reaching 17°C‑26°C on Wednesday, 16°C‑29°C on Thursday, and a maximum of 33°C on Friday as cloud cover decreased.

In addition to continental variations, the Brazilian Navy issued a swell warning for the coastal strip, forecasting waves up to 3 meters high along the capital’s shoreline. Official guidance recommends extra caution for beachgoers and residents of the coast during the marine agitation.

Information from G1, Rio Operations Center, Ilha Carioca.
